newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 54,000T of soybeans - trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 54,000T of soybeans - trade.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for 54,000 tonnes of soybeans this week while demand for corn will remain sluggish following the outbreak in March of hog foot-and-month disease, traders said on Monday.
A recent rally in soybean futures prices in Chicago prompted buyers to lock in supplies at current prices, the traders said.
"Buyers are likely to enter the (soybean) market since soybean prices seem to be on a uptrend," Steven Kuo, manager of Formosa Oilseed Processing Corp, said.
The July soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) hit a new contract high on Friday of US$8.96 a bushel, the highest level since the U.S. drought of 1988.
Kuo said $9.00 a bushel seems to be a short-term upper resistance level for soybean futures prices.
"A small price correction may soon take place if speculators begin to take profits," a trader said.
The Taiwan Breakfast Soybeans Procurement Association's Taichung division is also considering placing a tender for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. or South America soybeans, traders said.

The corn market should be quiet this week as feed producers try to trim their inventories after the foot-and-mouth outbreak ravaged the country's multi-billion dollar pork export industry and sharply reduced the demand for feed.
"It's going to be a quiet week for corn," a trader said.
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest freight fetched a quote of about $14.00 a tonne and Gulf of Mexico was seen at around $23.50 per tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
